title: Commit-window constrainer and granular burst reclaimer
author: Priya Khatri
description:
Motivation:
This PR introduces a lightweight enforcement layer (CommitWindowConstrain) for per-tenant commit windows and a GranularBurstReclaimer that reclaims unused burst credits more smoothly. The goal is to improve throughput guarantees for Dedicated tenants during sustained load while avoiding hard throttles that cause cascaded latency spikes.

What it changes (high level):
- New controller commit_window_controller: monitors tenant commit windows, underlying pool headroom, and soft-limits per-tenant based on recent usage profiles.
- GranularBurstReclaimer: returns unused burst credits back to the shared reservoir on a smoothed schedule (exponential decay + jitter) instead of instant forfeiture.
- New telemetry exports: 99/95/50 utilization percentiles for tenant pools, per-tenant headroom gauge, and a "reclaim_ramp" histogram to help correlate reclaim behavior with latency.
- Configuration surface: a new dedicated section in values.yaml and a runtime config map with knobs: commit_window_ms, reclaim_half_life_s, min_burst_floor, tenant_penalty_backoff.
- Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for controller logic, integration scenario using the perf-canary harness to validate throughput under synthetic long-tail sequences.

Why different from previous autoscalers:
Existing autoscalers optimize fleet size and coarse burst allocation. This work focuses on contract enforcement at the request admission level: rather than immediately blocking tenants that exceed burst expectations, the controller nudges soft-limits and reclaims credits gradually so downstream services see bounded, smooth degradations. It is intended to complement (not replace) existing reservation and warm-pool logic.

Checklist:
- [x] Implementation of controller + reclaimer
- [x] Unit tests for core decision functions
- [x] Telemetry integration and dashboards (draft)
- [x] Perf scenario validated end-to-end
- [x] Docs: runbook describing knobs and troubleshooting

Related: ENG-2345 (throughput-contracts iteration), ENG-2890 (observability for reclamation).

Backwards compatibility and rollout:
Behavior is gated behind a dedicated feature flag (commit_window_enforce=false by default). Chart / values.yaml ship with conservative defaults (commit_window_ms=2000, reclaim_half_life_s=120). We plan a canary rollout to two pools for 48h with close telemetry watch before enabling by default.

Notes for reviewers:
- The key heuristic lives in commit_window_controller.go (decision function is documented in comments). We opted for a conservative soft-penalty approach: reduce tenant burst cap by proportional delta and schedule reclaim; after repeated violations tenant_penalty_backoff grows.
- Reclaimer uses a token-based accounting system; the implementation includes a small deterministic jitter to avoid synchronized spikes across tenants.
- The telemetry names are intentionally explicit (tenant_headroom_gauge, tenant_util_p95, reclaim_ramp_ms_hist) — reviewer feedback on naming is welcome.

Small code excerpt (decision logic) for context:
```
// if tenant usage over window exceeds commit_window, compute soft reduce
if observed > config.commit_window_limit {
  penalty := min(max_penalty, (observed-config.commit_window_limit)/observed)
  new_cap := current_cap * (1 - penalty)
  scheduleReclaim(tenant, reclaim_half_life)
}
```

review_conversation:
Ethan Morales (2025-02-18): Nice direction. Can you justify the default reclaim_half_life_s=120? Feels long for some interactive workloads.

Priya Khatri (2025-02-18): The 120s default is conservative to avoid oscillation in production; we validated 30s/60s/120s in the canary and saw 30s caused sharp reclaim pulses under bursty traffic. We can expose an aggressive preset in values.yaml for low-latency tenants.

Lena Fischer (2025-02-19): Unit tests look good. Please add an assertion that tenant_penalty_backoff caps at the configured bound (to prevent runaway).

Priya Khatri (2025-02-19): Added cap and test; pushed a small follow-up commit.

Samir Patel (2025-02-19): Telemetry naming: tenant_util_p95 duplicates an existing metric name in a different package. Suggest prefixing with "dedicated_" to avoid scrape collisions.

Priya Khatri (2025-02-19): Renamed metrics to dedicated_tenant_util_p95, dedicated_tenant_headroom_gauge, and reclaim_ramp_ms_hist -> dedicated_reclaim_ramp_ms_hist. Updated dashboards reference.

Ethan Morales (2025-02-20): Integration runs looked stable for the canary pools. Approving pending squash and changelog entry.

release_notes:
- Add commit-window enforcement controller (feature-flagged); provides soft, proportional tenant cap reductions to protect throughput contracts.
- Add GranularBurstReclaimer to return unused burst credits on a smoothed schedule.
- Export dedicated_* tenant utilization and headroom metrics for improved observability.
- Default gated behind feature flag; canary rollout recommended before enabling cluster-wide.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag commit_window_enforce in chart to turn on controller; monitor dedicated_tenant_util_p95 and dedicated_reclaim_ramp_ms_hist. Recommended canary: 2 pools for 48h. If unstable, lower reclaim_half_life_s or increase min_burst_floor.
